Trust decision: the project fixes, in `multidict/_multilib/views.h`, that the identity/value refs taken while parsing each operand element must be released per iteration — two `Py_CLEAR` pairs in the reflected-union loop (views.h:565-576) and the subtraction loop (686-697), plus the missing `Py_CLEAR(arg)` on the subtraction `fail:` label (733-741).
`pattern_fit`: `injection_only` — Pattern A fails (all three source sites in one file/one module, no out-of-scope implementation; the pure-Python twin cannot leak) and Pattern B fails (the `^` route is covered transitively by the sub1 hunk; there is no unguarded route).
Strongest lever: the verification trap — the pinned leak script only uses empty operands (`tests/isolated/multidict_itemsview_set_operations.py:20,26`), so a solver can reproduce, "fully validate" and still leave non-empty operands leaking, or fix only the subtraction loop the report names.
Biggest red flag: `tiny_repo` (~20.4k lines across 56 files; a two-line-per-function fix in a repo small enough to read whole), with `j_multi_site=1` but `j_sibling_sites=no`.
